extracted.intended_audience: funders, reviewer trainers, and researchers interested in peer-review and bias in funding decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Reconstruction of the Swedish MRC mid-1990s three-dimensional scoring rubric for postdoctoral fellowships and the operational norms derived from empirical findings about gender and nepotism bias; useful for designing reviewer forms, training, and QA of panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific competence of the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record, publications, originality, intellectual quality (applicants scored on this dimension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored on a 0.0–4.0 scale in the Swedish MRC rubric; guidance suggests using observable indicators such as publication record and intellectual contributions rather than purely impressionistic judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the proposed methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigour, feasibility, adequacy of design, statistics, and controls of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 0.0–4.0; evaluate feasibility, experimental design quality, appropriateness of statistics and controls, and whether methods adequately address the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of the research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the question to the field and applicability of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 0.0–4.0; consider scientific importance, potential impact, and relevance to funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring aggregation to determine rank order
rubrics_metrics.description: The product (or in some panels the average) of the three dimension scores determined the funding rank order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify and document how dimension scores are combined (product vs. average) since aggregation method affects ranking sensitivity; ensure consistency across panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disregard applicant gender in assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should disregard the gender of the applicant when assessing competence; if unable to do so, they should recuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction to reviewers to avoid gender-based inference; recusal recommended when impartiality cannot be maintained. This norm is motivated by the finding that female applicants required substantially more publications to receive equal competence scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare personal or institutional affiliations (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare any personal or institutional affiliation with applicants and recuse where conflicts exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive disclosure of affiliations; recusal thresholds should be explicit (e.g., same institution, recent collaborator). The Swedish data showed an average affiliation 'bonus' (nepotism) of ~0.21 competence points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use objective bibliometric anchors for competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor objective measures (publication count, journal impact, citation count) rather than impressionistic judgements of 'scientific competence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt bibliometric anchors and clearly specified metrics to reduce subjective variance; calibrate how these metrics map onto the rubric scale (0–4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate scores against demographic/productivity baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate reviewer judgements against baselines such as productivity per year since PhD or demographic productivity norms where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use productivity-per-year or other time-normalised measures to avoid penalising career-stage differences; maintain demographic baselines to detect anomalous scoring patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymise applications where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should anonymise applications to reduce bias related to gender or affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible implement blinded review processes; note practical limits for some fields and career-stage assessments. Anonymisation is one structural response to the biases documented by Wennerås & Wold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement explicit conflict-of-interest exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should implement explicit COI exclusions rather than relying solely on reviewer self-management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and enforce COI policies (e.g., institutional, personal, co-authorship windows); use administrative checks in addition to reviewer declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit score distributions by demographic group
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit score distributions by demographic group as a routine quality-assurance step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly analyse panel scoring by gender, affiliation, and other demographics to detect systemic biases; use audits to inform corrective actions and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train panel members on documented bias (Wennerås–Wold case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train reviewers and panel members on the documented bias examples (the Wennerås & Wold result is cited as the canonical training case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include empirical examples of bias in mandatory training; emphasise concrete mitigation steps (blinding, COI management, bibliometric calibration, audit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical bias quantification (gender and nepotism effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wennerås & Wold findings: female applicants required ~2.5× the impact-factor-weighted publication count to receive the same competence score as men; applicants affiliated with a committee member received an average +0.21 competence points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these quantified effects as benchmarks when auditing panels and assessing whether corrective measures are effective; explicitly report effect sizes when examining disparities.
